sources.classification: labelled from the task code, 2026-10-10: Tacotron 2 is a text-to-mel-spectrogram model, so `tts`; precision fp32 (autocast disabled: the benchmark's --amp-run is not an argument of train.py); params counted from the layer shapes = embedding 75 776 (148 symbols x 512) + encoder 5 513 728 + decoder 18 255 505 + postnet 4 348 144 = 28 193 153; dataset_samples = lines of ljs_audio_text_train_subset_625_filelist.txt (whole clips; validation adds 100 clips per epoch)

measurements.source: Lambda, github.com/lambdal/deeplearning-benchmark, commit aa5addb6 (2025-12-17), pytorch/pytorch-train-throughput-fp16.csv, column tacotron2 (training throughput, mel frames/s), single-GPU rows run with batch 88 (pytorch/pytorch-train-bs-fp16.csv; config_pytorch_24GB.sh): 'RTX 4090' 32661; 'RTX 3090' 25018 ('LambdaCloud A10' ran batch 80 and is left out). The set is named fp16 after the CSV; the run computes in fp32 (see the task's docstring)
measurements.date: measurement dates are not in the CSV; repository snapshot 2025-12-17
measurements.hardware: Lambda's systems as named in the rows; NVIDIA NGC PyTorch container (version not recorded per row), LambdaLabsML/DeepLearningExamples branch lambda/benchmark
measurements.vram_gb_at_most_note: the run completed with batch 88 on 24 GB cards, so the peak is at most 24 GB
measurements.compute_ratio_note: throughput[RTX 4090] / throughput[GPU], one row per GPU. The run is 7 steps per epoch (625 clips, batch 88, last partial batch dropped). The throughput is the mean of per-step rates of the last epoch, timed after the batch is loaded: data loading is outside it
